name: zeek_run
description: Run the installed Zeek over a capture and read its logs back as records, with what ran recorded: the Zeek version as printed, the command, whether checksums were validated (-C is passed unless checksum_validation is true), and a policy script the tool writes into out_dir (by default one that loads policy/frameworks/files/hash-all-files; `policies` changes the list, an empty list loads nothing; a policy is a name Zeek resolves, never a path or a script from the evidence) with its path and SHA-256. Whether the installed build has a policy by that name, and which hash functions it computes, is not assumed: hashes_produced says whether any files.log record carries a hash value (hash_fields only names the columns, which a real install can have whether or not they were filled). The reader follows each log's own header (#separator, #set_separator, #empty_field, #unset_field, #fields, #types), \xNN escapes, sets and vectors as lists, typed numbers, and every time as raw text with a decoded `_utc` beside it; JSON logs are read too. A record that does not fit (a wrong column count, a value that is not its type, bad JSON or JSON nested deeper than 64 levels, no header, an empty or longer-than-8-character separator, empty-field or unset-field marker) is counted with its line and byte offset and kept whole in malformed-<log>.jsonl, and ok is false. Requested logs Zeek did not write are listed apart from logs written with no records; reporter, weird and capture_loss are always summarised (capture_loss exists only if its policy is loaded, so its absence is not a finding). conn.log rows are Zeek connections as Zeek defines them, not application data delivered. Every log stays whole in out_dir, named, and inline records are bounded by limit. SENSITIVE: logs can carry credentials, cookies and request URIs. The directory is private (0700/0600); inline records withhold secret-named fields and the hash of an object under 128 bytes, redact URLs, and scrub every other string except the typed kinds that are decided per log: Zeek's own identifiers (uid, fuid and the like), hashes and fingerprints, IP addresses in address fields, times, numbers, conn.log's service, conn_state and history (kerberos.log's service is a name from the wire and is scrubbed); a URL's host goes through the same rule as every other string (a token in a sub-domain is withheld), and so do the names under engine_diagnostics.weird.by_name (by shape: a short secret in free text is not recognised); run it as a job with secret_output: true. Zeek runs in the tool's own process group (the harness ending the tool ends Zeek; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP kill it), and timeout_seconds is held under the manifest's limit. A failing `zeek --version` makes the run not ok. Every answer carries status (complete when Zeek exited 0, every log was read through and every line fit its header; partial otherwise; failed for a refusal) and status_basis; exit 0 means the engine ran and the answer says whether it was whole, and a refusal is JSON and exit 1. Reading the logs back has a clock of its own that ends 30 seconds before the manifest's 1200, counted from the start of the tool, so the preflight and the time Zeek used are already out of it: a log still being read when it runs out is read in part (logs_read_in_part, read_to_the_end false, a problem names the line and byte), a log not reached is named in logs_not_read, every log is whole in out_dir, and the answer is partial (reading_cut_by_its_clock true). SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP kill Zeek and what it started, print partial JSON (the stage and the logs on disk) and exit 128 plus the signal; a signal that arrives while the final answer is written ends the tool with that one document. The names of the log files Zeek wrote are printed as Zeek chose them (the tool trusts the engine for them; a name chosen by the wire, which Zeek's own logs do not do, would be printed). A reporter message over 500 characters is shown cut with the count not shown and a pointer to reporter.log, where the whole is. The manifest declares secret_output: "required", so every job of this tool is run and sealed as secret output (the answer says so, secret_output_by: tool_manifest, and the process gets SECRET_OUTPUT=1). A stop that arrives before the script's first line has run (the interpreter's own start and its compile of the script) gets no answer: SIGTERM at a random offset of 0-250 ms after the start, 80 runs on one CPU (2026-11-01), left 14 runs without JSON, the latest at 40 ms, on a quiet host; a busy host sees more (misses up to about 80 ms were seen). A log's name is the engine's: it comes from Zeek's scripts and from the policies this tool loads, so only a hostile policy makes one token-shaped. A name shaped like a token or user-info is shown as withheld-NNNNNN in the keys of logs, in file, in malformed_files and in the lists of logs, the log is renamed to that in out_dir, and the real name is in zeek-log-names.jsonl in out_dir (mode 0600, named as log_names_file; the numbers follow the order of the real names); every other name is printed as Zeek wrote it. DRY RUN. dry_run: true (a boolean, default false; path is then refused as JSON) gives the engine's receipt without reading a capture: Zeek is started once, in out_dir, with the policy script and a small script of this tool's own that prints each script Zeek loads (from its zeek_script_loaded event), with no capture and no interface, and nothing is written outside out_dir. The answer has five parts. identities: the policy script's path, SHA-256 and size (the same bytes a run writes for the same policies), the version from zeek --version, zeek --help kept in zeek-help.txt, and rule_count null (Zeek loads scripts here, not signature rules, so there is no sid, rev or action to count). effective_configuration: the command, the exit code, and the scripts Zeek listed (the first 200 inline, each passed through the withholding block; every line in zeek-dry-run.stdout). script_load_status: for each requested policy whether Zeek listed it (null when Zeek listed nothing, which shows neither), and the first 10 lines of Zeek's output that name an error or a failure, each passed through the block as a whole and then cut to 300 characters. log_outputs: the logs the dry run itself left in out_dir (a token-shaped name is withheld and renamed as for a run); the streams a run would write are not listed, because they depend on the scripts and on traffic. not_covered: no ruleset or signature file ships with the pack and none is fetched; no download or update; no capture was read, so nothing says what the scripts would log. status is complete when Zeek exited 0, listed the scripts it loaded and every requested policy is among them; a Zeek that exits 0 and lists nothing (a build that does not raise the event) is partial, never an empty complete receipt. logs and limit are not used and are named in arguments_not_used. Zeek is given at most 120 seconds, and the whole dry run is held to timeout_seconds (10 to 1100, default 900); a stop (SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP) gives one JSON answer as for a run. A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 14: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape. A process Zeek leaves behind after it exits (a child that holds a log or one of the files the tool keeps (zeek.stdout, zeek.stderr), in the tool's process group or in a session of its own, or one that holds no descriptor) is stopped, killed and reaped by the shared process block's settle() before the logs are listed, read or counted; one found, or a host where the absence of one cannot be proven (not Linux, PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER refused), makes the answer at most partial (program_group.left_behind, program_group.unproven and a line under problems), and the logs are then what the leftover had written when it was ended. A process that is no descendant of Zeek (started through a service manager) is not found. The same holds for dry_run, whose listing and logs are read after the same settle.

path.description: A pcap or pcapng file (required, and refused when dry_run is true)

dry_run.description: true gives the engine receipt (identities, effective configuration, load status, log outputs, what is not covered) without reading a capture; default false. path is refused with it

out_dir.description: An empty directory under work/ (in a job, under $OUT; work/<your id>/name is mapped to $OUT/name) where Zeek runs and its logs land. It is private (0700, files 0600)

logs.description: Which logs to return inline, e.g. ["conn","dns","ssl"] (default: every log written). A name Zeek did not write is listed in logs_requested_not_written; reporter, weird and capture_loss are summarised regardless

limit.description: Maximum records per log returned inline (default 200); the whole log is the file named in its entry, and omitted says how many were not returned

timeout_seconds.description: Kill Zeek, and everything it started, after this long (10 to 1100 seconds, default 900), so that this tool stops Zeek before the 1200-second limit does

policies.description: Zeek policy names to load through the script the tool writes (default ["policy/frameworks/files/hash-all-files"]; [] loads none). Names only: a path, a name that climbs out of Zeek's script path or one under inputs/ is refused

checksum_validation.description: Leave Zeek's checksum validation on (default false: -C is passed, and the answer says checksums were not validated)
